the range's pilasters and the colonnade's columns heavier than built
a light iron cresting along the transept's level crest from its hipped end to the nave, a finial over the transept's end and a small ornament over the nave's apex (T-3164)
the east range's coping: plain stone in both pictures, as built (an earlier reading called for iron cresting along it)

Nothing to build on the range.

the glass reads pale (the sky in it) on the transept, the drum and the domes
differences.how: T-3179: those parts, which stand outside the nave's one transparent envelope, take an opaque glazing toned pale (glass_sky) instead of the kit's dark substitute; colour itself is not shown (a monochrome picture)

differences.what: the glasshouses' south and west sides and the ranges' roofs behind their parapets

differences.what: the lodge's lower hipped roof over the front's west part (plate x 1055-1135), which the render carries on as the one hipped roof

Read in both pictures: the part's quoined east return (plate x 1052-1058, Lowe x 660-668), its eave a few px over the loggia block's (plate y 705-712 against 718, Lowe 396-398 against 402) and its north-east hip rising from the return to about the deck's height (plate x 1058,712 to 1118,625; Lowe x 667,397 to 703,345). Through the plate's camera the built hip runs x 1046,716 to 1101,633 and the return x 1044-1053, about 10 px east of the picture's, under the 0.3 m bar at this distance along the line of sight; the picture's part beyond x 1085 is behind the render's transept arm (that arm's east end is the pavilion record's own item)

differences.what: a dark pointed form over the west part's roof at its ridge, plate x 1116-1142 at its foot rising to a point at about y 562, beside the deck's north-west spire: built as a slated spirelet 0.9 m square on the ridge's middle with an iron spike, its point a little over the spire's, as the plate draws it (T-3164)
the dome and its drum stand about 25 px (0.6 m) west of the plate's (Lowe shows the same, about 20 px)

Read on the same cameras at that depth, the drum's top is 9.7-9.8 m (it was 10.0), the dome's crown 12.3 m on the plate and 12.7 m in Lowe (it was 13.1; built 12.5) and the finial's tip 13.6-13.8 m (it was a 0.5 m stick; built as the turned finial both pictures show, a flared foot, a bulb, a neck, a knob and a spike, to 13.75 m). The render's dome now lies on the plate's within about 5 px across and 10 px in height

The leaves' cutting is under the bar (L-pullman-gate-1800-calumet-3164)
